Thought: Isobutyl formate is an ester with the formula (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OCHO. When esters react with water, they undergo hydrolysis. Ester hydrolysis produces a carboxylic acid and an alcohol. In this case, isobutyl formate would hydrolyze to form formic acid (HCOOH, a carboxylic acid) and isobutyl alcohol ((CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH).

The question is asking about which molecule results from this reaction. Since one of the products is formic acid, which is a carboxylic acid, the answer is A. Carboxylic acid.
